chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Sabbah ibn Sayyabah who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when it was asked him: 'Does the adulterer remain a believer while committing the sin?' He said: 'No. When he is on the act, faith is stripped from him, and when he finishes, it is returned to him.' It was asked: 'What if he intends to do it again?' He said: 'How many are those who intend to do it again but do not.'
ai.seo_question: Is a person considered a believer while committing the sin of adultery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the transient nature of faith during the act of adultery, noting that *iman* is stripped from the adulterer while the act is ongoing and restored upon its completion. This highlights the distinction between the state of the heart during the sin and the enduring reality of belief, while also observing the human tendency to intend repetition without following through. The commentary underscores the dynamic interplay between action and spiritual status in Shia jurisprudence.
